transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-09-15
Start: 11:00 AM PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Kim (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, Fjord), Tom Brennan (Infra Lead, Fjord), Sara Cho (Procurement, Fjord)

Summary: quick renewal/expansion check in; customer nearing end of current term (30 days), exploring dedicated capacity and EU region, need benchmarks and SLA to sign 12-month extension.

[00:00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, we got Lena, Tom, Sara, Marcus and me. how's every- how's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Lena: good, thanks. busy quarter but excited to chat.
[00:00:15] Ava: Great. we wanted to recap where you are with Redwood and go over the expansion asks dedicated capacity, EU region, and extension options. this should be pretty actionable.
[00:00:30] Tom: yeah thanks. so short context, we've been on the hosted plan for 9 months, using it for customer-facing summarization and chatops. volume's up about 3x since q2 and the variability is starting to impact p99 latency during peaks.
[00:00:45] Marcus: when you say p99 are we talking tail latency for the chat endpoint or for embedding pipelines?
[00:00:52] Tom: mostly chat/generation, embeddings are heavy but batched overnight. the chat spikes are what cause tail issues.
[00:01:05] Lena: also regulatory - a subset of EU customers requires data to stay in EU region, so we need an EU deploy or private tenancy for that traffic.
[00:01:15] Ava: Understood. high-level we see two levers: Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, and/or adding EU region in our hosted footprint or Private for stricter residency. what are your priorities - latency or data residency first?
[00:01:30] Tom: latency first for the public customers, residency for financial customers. ideally both.
[00:01:40] Sara: procurement note - we prefer a 12-month extension if pricing is favorable and there is a migration credit.
[00:01:48] Ava: Got it. we'll propose a 12-month renewal with an expansion tier for Dedicated and a one-time migration credit.

[00:02:10] Marcus: quick technical check: what models are you running in prod today?
[00:02:15] Lena: mostly open models - Llama2 variants and a couple smaller fine-tuned checkpoints. In production we use Redwood's hosted API with some caching at the app level. we do a short-term prefix cache but not full KV cache.
[00:02:30] Marcus: okay, good. for Dedicated we recommend enabling KV cache + longer prefix caching to reduce token cost and p99. can you share request size distribution and sequence lengths?
[00:02:45] Tom: sure, I'll drop the last 7 days of logs - average seq length ~320, 95th 1,200 during agent flows. QPS baseline 60, peaks up to 220 for a 10-min window.
[00:03:00] Marcus: that's helpful - Dedicated cluster sizing will use those peaks; also batching behavior matters. are you currently using our streaming endpoint?
[00:03:08] Lena: yes for chat. streaming is on.
[00:03:12] Marcus: great - streaming + KV cache + dedicated GPUs will move your p99 down a lot. we can show numbers in the benchmark.

[00:03:35] Tom: on region setup - what's the difference between a hosted EU region versus Private VPC in EU? partly curious on networking and certs.
[00:03:45] Ava: hosted EU is fully managed - data processed in EU region and covered by our standard controls. Private VPC is customer-controlled networking, we can run control plane in our region but keep inference in your VPC/region; tends to be used for strict compliance.
[00:04:00] Sara: does Private require on-prem or can it be cloud VPC?
[00:04:05] Ava: cloud VPC is supported. on-prem is possible but longer lead time.

[00:04:22] Lena: security-wise they asked about SOC2, kms, and audit logs - can we get the docs?
[00:04:28] Ava: yes, we'll send SOC2 report and our KMS integration notes; audit log options are standard. Marcus can share the logging retention and format.
[00:04:38] Marcus: note that we support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) for Private and Dedicated via our key wrap flow. the audit logs include per-request metadata.

[00:05:05] Tom: cost question - what's the delta from hosted to Dedicated for our footprint? we want predictable monthly commit but also some burst capacity.
[00:05:12] Ava: roughly, Dedicated with reserved commit reduces per-token unit cost by about 30-45% depending on utilization; there's a fixed cluster fee. for your peaks we can size a base pool with burstable nodes. i'll send a model specific price sheet.
[00:05:30] Sara: procurement wants a line item for an integration/migration credit - is that standard?
[00:05:35] Ava: we can offer a one-time migration credit for expansion deals over certain commit thresholds; we'll include that in the proposal.

[00:05:55] Lena: timeline - our current hosted contract ends in 30 days. we need final terms and an initial benchmark before commit. can you run a benchmark to show p99 improvements in EU and US?
[00:06:05] Marcus: yes. propose we run a 1-hour benchmark on a Dedicated replica in EU-west and US-west using your traffic replay. we'll measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per token.
[00:06:18] Tom: we'll provide traffic replay and the black-box topologies. can you also instrument with our datadog agent?
[00:06:25] Marcus: we have integrations; for Dedicated we can ship telemetry to your Datadog instance - need API key and endpoint.
[00:06:32] Sara: is there any SLA delta for Dedicated? procurement wants hard p99 targets.
[00:06:38] Ava: Dedicated has SLA options; for hard p99 we typically include an SLA tier with uptime and latency SLOs. Marcus will follow up with the SLA doc and options.

[00:07:05] Tom: on region failover - if EU goes down does traffic route to US? we can't have EU-residency traffic cross borders.
[00:07:14] Marcus: we can set routing policies by customer segment - EU traffic can fail to a cold backup but we'd flag for residency concerns; automatic cross-border failover would violate residency. so for EU-residency flows we recommend Private or dedicated EU nodes with manual failover.
[00:07:30] Lena: that sounds fine. for most EU traffic we want strict residency, so Private VPC in eu-west or hosted EU with contracts is acceptable if contracts are explicit.

[00:07:50] Ava: ok next - contract length and pricing. Sara, you mentioned 12 months as preferred?
[00:07:55] Sara: yes, 12 months with the expansion tier and migration credit; procurement also wants a 60-day termination notice clause and a cap on price increases.
[00:08:08] Ava: we can do 12 months, include a migration credit, and standard price protection clauses; final legal will confirm precise language.

[00:08:25] Marcus: action from our side: we'll provision a Dedicated eval cluster in EU-west for the benchmark. need Tom's logs, Datadog access, and a list of models to test.
[00:08:35] Tom: i'll upload logs to the shared drive and send the datadog key via secure link.
[00:08:40] Marcus: perfect. we'll also collect traces and token cost estimates so you can compare.

[00:09:05] Lena: one thing - we've been experimenting with quantization on smaller models; will Redwood support q4 and q8 variants on Dedicated?
[00:09:13] Marcus: yes, our runtime supports quantized variants, though exact perf depends on model architecture. we'll note recommendations in the benchmark. sometimes q4 gives big gains for throughput but can change output quality; we'll run QA on your prompt set.

[00:09:35] Sara: procurement process - once we get pricing and SLA, we want a 1-week review period. can you tune dates so we can sign before current contract ends?
[00:09:45] Ava: yes we'll move quickly: pricing out today, SLA doc and benchmark plan by 9/22, benchmark run next week, and a proposal by 9/24.

[00:10:05] Tom: technical question - do you support bring-your-own-VPC peering for Private? our security team will want to peer and manage routes.
[00:10:14] Marcus: we support VPC peering and PrivateLink style connections; we'll provide network runbook.

[00:10:30] Lena: also curious about tracing - does Redwood provide per-call logs for auditing?
[00:10:36] Marcus: yes, per-request audit logs and optional payload redaction. retention policies configurable on Dedicated/Private.

[00:11:00] Sara: about pricing tiers - can we get a table showing delta at 1x, 3x, 5x usage? procurement likes scenario-based pricing.
[00:11:08] Ava: yes, we'll include scenario-based cost modeling in the proposal.

[00:11:25] Tom: one more - backup and retention for KV cache? if we rely on caching, what's restore behavior across restarts?
[00:11:33] Marcus: KV cache is warm but not persisted across cluster rebuilds by default; we can set up prefix caching and optional persistent cache layers depending on the workflow. we'll include options.

[00:11:55] Lena: any blockers from Redwood side for a 12-month extension?
[00:12:00] Ava: no blockers - main items are the benchmark results and agreed pricing/SLA.

[00:12:20] (minutes pass; discussion about scheduling details and logistics)
[00:22:40] Marcus: i've noted: need traffic replay, datadog API, list of models, and acceptance test prompts.
[00:22:48] Tom: i'll get those by EOD tomorrow.

[00:25:00] Sara: quick legal question - do you support EU data processing addendum (DPA)?
[00:25:06] Ava: yes, we have a DPA and standard model clauses; we'll attach to the proposal.

[00:28:15] Lena: could you include a recommended Dedicated cluster size for our peaks? even a rough starting number helps planning.
[00:28:23] Marcus: based on the 220 QPS peaks and seq lengths, i'd start with a 4-GPU baseline (A100 class equiv) with 2 burst nodes. that's conservative; the benchmark will refine it.

[00:29:05] Tom: ok that seems reasonable. what's the lead time to stand up a Dedicated eval cluster in EU-west?
[00:29:12] Marcus: we can provision an eval in 48-72 hours for benchmark purposes; production Dedicated can take 2-3 weeks for full provisioning and networking.

[00:30:00] Sara: one last procurement ask - can you include a short term discount if we sign the 12-month by next week?
[00:30:07] Ava: we can propose a signing discount tier; i'll include that in the proposal.

[00:30:30] (small side conversation about billing cadence)
[00:33:00] Ava: ok let's recap and confirm next steps.
[00:33:05] Ava: action items: Ava will send pricing and draft proposal with migration credit and signing discount by 2027-09-20; Marcus will share SLA doc and provision an eval cluster for benchmarks and share the benchmark plan by 2027-09-22; Tom will share logs, datadog keys, and models by 2027-09-18.
[00:33:25] Sara: sounds good. procurement will review within 1 week of receiving the proposal.
[00:33:35] Lena: we'll schedule the benchmark window for next week - prefer Wed or Thu.
[00:33:40] Marcus: i'll send a poll for Wed/Thu times.

[00:34:00] Ava: thanks everyone - we'll follow up in email with links to SOC2, DPA, SLA, and the pricing sheet.
[00:34:10] Tom: thanks.
[00:34:12] Sara: thanks.
[00:34:15] Lena: thanks all.

[00:34:30] (call ends)

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings - e.g., "KV cash" in a couple places from the auto transcript; speaker labels were cleaned but may not match exact utterances.
